name: All-Clad D3 12" Fry Pan (or D5)
desc: The best all-purpose stainless steel frying pan, for searing, pan sauces and anything that goes into the oven.
tip: Amazon has dropped it to ~$80–90 several times. All-Clad factory-seconds sales are another good option.

name: All-Clad D3 3 qt Saucier
desc: A rounded-bottom saucepan that's easy to whisk in, for risotto, custards, sauces and grains.
where: All-Clad Factory Seconds / Sur La Table
tip: Factory-seconds sales (allcladfactoryseconds.com) regularly have D3 sauciers around $75–$90.

name: OXO Good Grips Pro 12" Nonstick Fry Pan
desc: A big, reliable nonstick pan for eggs, fish and pancakes that won't break the bank when it's time to replace it.
tip: The Pro hard-anodized line is the one that tests well. Skip the it.com 'OXO' sites that showed up in search. They look like scam storefronts.

name: OXO Good Grips Pro 8" Nonstick Fry Pan
desc: A small nonstick pan sized for one or two eggs or a single omelet.
where: Amazon / Home Depot / Sur La Table
tip: Often $22 at Amazon. The 8" + 10" 2-pack at Sur La Table can be better value.

name: Cuisinart Chef's Classic 12 qt Stock Pot
desc: A tall, induction-ready pot for stock, pasta, corn and big batches of soup.
where: ATK test price · Sur La Table $48–$65 by size
tip: ATK's induction-compatible pick. Upgrade: Tramontina 12 qt tri-ply (~$65). Commercial: Vollrath Tribute (~$195).

name: Le Creuset Signature Round Dutch Oven, 5.5 qt / 7.25 qt
desc: The classic enameled cast-iron Dutch oven for braises, stews, chili and no-knead bread.
where: Amazon (5.5 qt in White/Oyster) · Sur La Table $364+
tip: Color drives the price: some colors drop to ~$240 on Amazon. Le Creuset outlets and Black Friday are the other times to buy. List is ~$420 / ~$480.

name: Nordic Ware Naturals Half Sheet, 2-pack
desc: Heavy-gauge bare aluminum pans that won't warp, for roasting vegetables and baking cookies.
tip: Amazon has sold it for ~$17 in the past (Slickdeals).

name: Nordic Ware Naturals Quarter Sheet, 2-pack
desc: A smaller sheet pan for toaster-oven batches, prep staging and small roasts.

name: USA Pan 1 lb Loaf Pan (×2)
desc: Corrugated, nonstick pans that release sandwich bread, banana bread and pound cake cleanly.
tip: Sur La Table often has 20%-off codes (SAVE20 at the time of checking).

name: French Tapered Rolling Pin (maple)
desc: A tapered handle-less pin that gives you better feel and control for pie crusts and cookie dough.
tip: The J.K. Adams pin, an ATK pick, is similar. Its Cook's Warehouse page is gone, so this links to Sur La Table's version.

name: OXO Good Grips 2-Piece Chef's Squeeze Bottle Set
desc: Restaurant-style bottles for oils, dressings and sauces, with easy-to-control pouring.

name: The Chef's Press 3-pc Starter Set (Bruce Hill)
desc: Perforated weights that press down on bacon, burgers, chicken and sandwiches for even browning and crisp edges.
tip: I couldn't find a US retailer price. This is converted from CAD. Also check thechefspress.com.

name: Earlywood Spatula Set
desc: Handmade hardwood flat-edged spatulas that scrape fond and won't scratch pans.
tip: The Flat Sauté set is the classic starter.

name: OXO Good Grips Bench Scraper
desc: A stainless steel blade for portioning dough, scooping chopped food and cleaning the counter.

name: John Boos R02 Maple Board, 24"×18"×1.5"
desc: A thick, heirloom-quality maple board that's gentle on knife edges and lasts decades.
tip: Restaurant suppliers (KaTom, GoFoodservice) tend to beat kitchen retailers on Boos.

name: Winco CBWT-1824 Poly Board, 24"×18"
desc: A cheap, dishwasher-safe commercial poly board, good for raw meat and messy jobs.
tip: Check the shipping cost, since it's a big, heavy board.

name: Wüsthof Classic 8" Chef's Knife
desc: A durable, full-tang German chef's knife that handles almost every cutting task.
tip: Check camelcamelcamel for the Amazon price history before you buy.

name: Tojiro Bread Slicer 235mm (F-737)
desc: A long, sharp serrated knife that slices crusty bread without crushing it, at a bargain price.

name: Cuisinart Custom 14-Cup Food Processor (DFP-14BCNY)
desc: A powerful 14-cup workhorse for shredding, slicing, dough and pesto.
tip: Amazon has gone as low as ~$150.

name: KitchenAid Artisan 5 qt Tilt-Head or 5.5 qt Bowl-Lift (KSM55)
desc: The standard stand mixer for bread dough, cookies and whipped cream, with a huge range of attachments.
tip: The bowl-lift is the better deal right now. The Artisan has hit ~$240–$250 on past Lowe's/Amazon sales.

name: Breville Smart Oven (BOV800XL)
desc: A countertop convection oven that toasts, bakes and roasts well enough to sub for a small second oven.
tip: It goes on sale often, so don't pay $250.

name: Vitamix 5-Speed Immersion Blender
desc: A powerful immersion blender for puréeing soup right in the pot, smoothies and emulsions.

name: Zojirushi Micom 5.5-Cup Rice Cooker (NL-EAC10WA)
desc: A fuzzy-logic rice cooker that gets white, brown and sushi rice right every time.
tip: The NL-AAC10 is a near-twin at a similar price.

name: Chef'n FreshForce Lemon Squeezer
desc: A double-gear squeezer that gets the most juice from a lemon with the least effort.

name: OXO Good Grips Y-Peeler
desc: A sharp, comfortable Y-peeler that makes fast work of carrots, potatoes and squash.
tip: The 3-pc set (straight, serrated, julienne) costs about the same as a single peeler.

name: Presto 07046 Tilt 'n Drain Big Griddle
desc: An extra-large electric griddle that tilts to drain grease, for pancakes, bacon and eggs for a crowd.

name: Cuisinart Double Flip Belgian Waffle Maker (WAF-F20)
desc: A rotating Belgian waffle maker that makes two thick, crisp waffles at once.
tip: Williams Sonoma lists it at $119.95, which is the high end.
